statement: Define M for any list xs of pairwise distinct integers by: M([]) = Null; if xs is nonempty, let k be the unique index with 0 <= k < len(xs) and xs[k] = max(xs), and set M(xs) = Node(xs[k], M(xs[0..k)), M(xs[k+1..len(xs)))). Here xs[a..b) is the sublist of elements at indices a through b-1. Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, r = M(nums).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, there exist v, L, and R such that r = Node(v, L, R), and v = max(nums[0], ..., nums[len(nums)-1]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, count_nodes(r) = len(nums), where count_nodes(Null) = 0 and count_nodes(Node(v, L, R)) = 1 + count_nodes(L) + count_nodes(R).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, inorder(r) = [nums[0], nums[1], ..., nums[len(nums)-1]], where inorder(Null) = [] and inorder(Node(v, L, R)) = inorder(L) ++ [v] ++ inorder(R).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, for every node u of r with value v, every node value w occurring in the left subtree of u or in the right subtree of u satisfies w < v. Occurrence in a subtree is defined recursively through child subtrees.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Let k be the unique index with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = max(nums). Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, r = Node(nums[k], L, R) for some L and R, and the values occurring in L are exactly the values nums[i] with 0 <= i < k, each occurring exactly once; the values occurring in R are exactly the values nums[i] with k < i < len(nums), each occurring exactly once.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Let k be the unique index with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = max(nums). Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r = Node(v, L, R), count_nodes(L) = k and count_nodes(R) = len(nums) - 1 - k, where count_nodes(Null) = 0 and count_nodes(Node(w, A, B)) = 1 + count_nodes(A) + count_nodes(B).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, for every node u of r, if s is the list of values in the subtree rooted at u in inorder (left subtree, then the value of u, then right subtree), then there exist integers a and b with 0 <= a <= b <= len(nums) such that s = [nums[a], nums[a+1], ..., nums[b-1]]. Here the list is empty when a = b.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, the following holds for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) for which nums[i] is not the maximum value of nums. Let jL be the largest index j < i with nums[j] > nums[i], if such an index exists, and let jR be the smallest index j > i with nums[j] > nums[i], if such an index exists. At least one of jL and jR exists. Let p be nums[jL] if only jL exists, nums[jR] if only jR exists, and min(nums[jL], nums[jR]) if both exist. Then in r the node with value nums[i] has a parent with value p; that is, the node with value p has as a left child or a right child the node with value nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, for every integer x, x occurs as the value of some node of r if and only if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = x.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, height(r) <= len(nums) <= 1000, where height(Null) = 0 and height(Node(v, L, R)) = 1 + max(height(L), height(R)).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, r = Node(nums[0], Null, Null).

statement: Let k be the unique index with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = max(nums). Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, write r = Node(v, L, R). Then L = Null if and only if k = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Let k be the unique index with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = max(nums). Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, write r = Node(v, L, R). Then R = Null if and only if k = len(nums) - 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, for every index j with 0 <= j < len(nums), the node with value nums[j] has right child Null; its left child is Null when j = 0 and is the node with value nums[j-1] when j > 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct. Additionally, for every i with 0 <= i < n - 1, nums[i] < nums[i+1].

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, for every index j with 0 <= j < len(nums), the node with value nums[j] has left child Null; its right child is Null when j = len(nums) - 1 and is the node with value nums[j+1] when j < len(nums) - 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; and nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct. Additionally, for every i with 0 <= i < n - 1, nums[i] > nums[i+1].

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, r is the unique binary tree such that inorder(r) = [nums[0],...,nums[n-1]] and every node's value is strictly greater than every value in its left and right subtrees. (This makes explicit that the combination of spec_4, spec_5 and spec_6 already pins down the answer uniquely, so no other tree could also be returned.)
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; nums[0],...,nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, for every node u of r let [a,b) be the contiguous index range whose inorder values are the values of u's subtree (as in spec_9); then the subtree rooted at u equals M(nums[a..b)), where M is the function defined in spec_1. This strengthens S9 from a mere contiguity/inorder statement to a full structural statement at every node.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; nums[0],...,nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever construct_maximum_binary_tree(nums) returns a result r, no value is duplicated: for every integer x, the number of nodes of r whose value is x equals 1 if there is an index i with nums[i] = x, and equals 0 otherwise. (S11 only gives set membership; this states the exact multiplicity, which together with no extra nodes forbids any repeated or spurious node.)
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000; nums[0],...,nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct.
